_readme: Applet capabilities that are NOT declared as AppletAIActions in Swift. portalApplets merges this over the built-in action catalog, so an applet driven by tunnel commands (LoopStar) or with capability that exists in Swift but is not yet exposed (MapGuide, AudioLibrary) still shows up when an agent asks what the app can do. CONTENT per RULE #1 — add an applet here by PR, no rebuild.

_statusMeaning.callable: Works today. The example payload is real and has been run.
_statusMeaning.planned: The capability EXISTS in Swift but has no agent-reachable verb yet. Tell the user it is not available rather than attempting it; see docs/APPLET_VERB_SCOPING.md for the roadmap.

applets.summary: Music sequencer and generative jam station. Genre packs, tempo, key, chords, arrangement, and audio export.

capabilities.description: The 24 generative genres you can ask for, plus which one is active. Also reachable as the raw diagLoopStar action.
Switch the generative genre, e.g. trap, jazz, lofi, house. Unknown names return the valid list. Also reachable as the raw diagLoopStar action.
Set an absolute tempo in BPM. Clamped to 50-150% of the pack's base tempo; the response reports the BPM actually applied. Also reachable as the raw diagLoopStar action.
Set the session key. Also reachable as the raw diagLoopStar action.
Everything at once: active genre, pack, tempo, lane states, transport position, chord label. Also reachable as the raw diagLoopStar action.

Render the arrangement to a bar-exact WAV and file it in the Audio Library. Needs at least one arrangement section; the WAV is probed for silence before it is filed. Returns an openable audio.track entity.

applets.notes: LoopStar declares no AppletAIActions, so it is invisible to the built-in action catalog despite being the most capable applet in the app. Audio must be verified BY EAR - the diagnostic meters read 0 even while sound is playing.

applets.summary: Place discovery, saved places, and narrated audio tours. Tours sync to iOS.

capabilities.description: Find sights, restaurants, and beaches for a destination. AudioTourGeneratorService.generateStops already builds Wikipedia-enriched, category-filtered POI tours - it simply has no agent-reachable verb.
Assemble discovered places into a tour. Tours already CloudKit-sync to iOS, so an agent-created tour would reach the phone for free.

applets.notes: The highest-value planned work in the app: the capability is built and syncs to iOS, but nothing can reach it. See docs/APPLET_VERB_SCOPING.md journey A.

applets.summary: Recorded and generated audio, organised in folders, with transcription. Tracks sync to iOS as CloudKit assets.

capabilities.description: Turn text into a saved audio track. AppleSpeechRenderer.renderToFile is already static and headless; only the verb is missing.
List tracks and folders. Store methods exist.

applets.notes: Audio placed here reaches iOS automatically (CKAsset sync), which makes it the best destination for agent-generated audio.

applets.summary: Cross-applet asset handoff. The noun that lets one applet's output become another applet's input across two separate CLI invocations — the gap CLI_PORTAL_ARCHITECTURE §2 names for the noir-ToonStudio case.

capabilities.description: Compose music from a natural-language brief in LoopStar and return a portable assetID. Drives the OPEN LoopStar window when there is one; warns in `warnings` when it had to use a headless instance (invariant R4). Verifies the WAV's duration and peak before registering — a silent render fails the verb rather than returning a handle to nothing.

example.brief: noir jazz, 92bpm, 8-bar intro then a 16-bar A section

capabilities.description: Attach a composed audio asset to a ToonStudio project as a per-scene music cue. Copies into the project's audio directory (guarding source == destination), REPLACES stock generator cues rather than only filling empty slots, and returns the project with an open deep link. Paired check: diagToonLint.

List, resolve or sweep asset handles. An assetID is the only thing that crosses the CLI boundary — container paths never leave the app because they differ per build lane and are frequently unreadable by the caller. `verified` is tri-state: true / false / null for not-yet-checked.
